steps.rule: +1 accessory dwelling unit on a lot with a conforming single-family house. It must sit behind the house and outside required yards. Footprint is capped at 25% of the house's gross floor area or 750 sq ft, whichever is less. The property must have a homestead exemption (or a pending application), so the owner must live there. Attached units cannot have an inside door to the house. Deed restrictions and HOA rules can still bar it.

params.max_height: 15 ft within 5 ft of a lot line; taller units meet the house's setbacks and cannot be taller than the house (Sec. 656.403(d))

steps.note: The code allows accessory uses in all districts and ties the ADU to a conforming single-family dwelling. by_district lists the covered districts that permit single-family dwellings; the code itself gives no district list. The 750 sq ft cap is on footprint, not total floor area.

steps.rule: Two or more units on one lot (the code calls any building with more than one unit multiple-family) need 6,000 sq ft for the first two units, then the added area per unit. RMD-B, RMD-C and RMD-D also need 60 ft of width; CRO and RO need 50 ft. RMD-A does not permit multiple-family.
steps.section: Sec. 656.306 A.II (d)(3); Sec. 656.311 A.III (e), A.IV (e); Sec. 656.1601 (Dwelling, multiple-family)

steps.rule: Townhomes sold on their own lots: 1,500 sq ft lot, 15 ft wide (25 ft for end units, 20 ft in a two-unit building), 70% coverage, 35 ft height. Overall density follows the district's multiple-family rule. Permitted in RLD-TNH and RMD-A to RMD-D.

Cottages (RMD-A to RMD-D): 1,500 sq ft lot, 25 ft wide, 70% coverage, 80% impervious surface, up to the units the district density allows. Outside the Urban Priority Area and urban area, AGR, RR and RLD land cannot be rezoned to permit cottages.

Single-family house: 2 spaces. Multiple-family: 1.5 spaces for a studio or one-bedroom of 500 sq ft or less, 1.75 for a larger one-bedroom, 2 for a two-bedroom, plus 0.25 per bedroom over two. Dens and studies count as bedrooms. Townhome, cottage or condominium: 2 spaces per unit plus 1 guest space per 3 units. Housing for the elderly: 1 space per 2 units.

Ask for the next district up. The new district must fit the parcel's land use category in the 2045 Comprehensive Plan: RMD-A and RMD-B are secondary districts in Low Density Residential (up to 7 units per acre in the category text); RMD-C, RMD-D and RHD need a Medium or High Density Residential category, which is a separate land use amendment.
steps.section: Sec. 656.304 B, 656.305 A and B, 656.306 A and B, 656.307 A (primary and secondary districts by land use category)

steps.rule: state laws that change what the city code allows on this lot

items.text: Florida Live Local Act. On land zoned commercial, industrial or mixed use, the city must allow multifamily or mixed-use rental housing if at least 40% of the units are affordable rentals for at least 30 years (mixed-use projects: at least 65% of floor area residential). The city cannot hold density below the highest density it allows anywhere, FAR below 150% of its highest, or height below the tallest allowed within 1 mile or 3 stories, whichever is higher. Approval is administrative. Height can be limited next to single-family neighborhoods. Excluded: airport-impacted areas and working waterfront in industrial zones. Expires October 1, 2033. Affordable is defined in s. 420.0004 (not read here).

Much of Jacksonville sits on the St. Johns River, its creeks and the coast. Check the FEMA flood zone (the parcel layer carries FLD_ZONE; FEMA NFHL layer 28 has the polygons). Zones A, AE and VE mean elevation rules and flood insurance.

Riverside, Avondale, Springfield and other historic districts need a Certificate of Appropriateness before building or demolition. Springfield has its own zoning districts (RMD-S, CRO-S, CN-S, CCG-S), which this file does not cover.
Florida has no statewide ADU mandate. The city rule (Sec. 656.403(g)) applies, and it needs a homestead exemption on the property.
Gross density cannot exceed the Comprehensive Plan land use category density, even where the zoning lot size would allow more (Sec. 656.305 A.II (h)).
Lot coverage is also limited by the impervious surface ratios in Sec. 654.129 (subdivision code), which were not read for this file.
ADU permit applications must certify that deed restrictions or HOA rules allow the unit (Sec. 656.403(g)(8)).
Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, Neptune Beach and Baldwin are in Duval County but have their own zoning codes. They are filtered out by city.
